About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
We are looking for research engineers to build the safety and oversight mechanisms that govern how our models handle biological knowledge. As a bio safety researcher, you will spend your time: designing and running capability evaluations against frontier models, generating and curating training data for our safety classifiers, training and iterating on those classifiers alongside our ML engineers, and measuring how they hold up against adversarial pressure in production traffic.
This work sits at the intersection of applied ML and biosecurity. You will help define what responsible AI safety looks like in the biological domain, translating threat models into evals, datasets, and deployed systems. The core technical tension you will own is precision: safeguards need to be robust against sophisticated actors while staying out of the way of the far larger population of legitimate researchers using Claude to accelerate life sciences work. Getting that tradeoff right is an empirical problem, and you will be the person measuring it.
You do not need to be an ML researcher today. We are looking for strong scientific programmers with real depth in modern biology who want to bring that depth to bear on model evaluation and classifier development.
Key responsibilities
Design, build, and run capability evaluations to assess what new models can do in the biological domain, and turn results into concrete deployment recommendations
Develop training and evaluation datasets for our safety classifiers, working with internal and external threat modeling experts to ground them in realistic risk
Train, tune, and iterate on safety classifiers with ML engineers, optimizing jointly for adversarial robustness and low false-positive rates
Build the tooling and pipelines that make evaluation and classifier development fast and repeatable
Analyze classifier and eval performance against production traffic, identify gaps, and prioritize improvements
Design and run red-teaming and stress-testing of safeguards as threats, models, and product surfaces evolve
Partner with Research, Product, and Policy teams to embed biological safety throughout the model development lifecycle
Contribute to external communications including model cards, blog posts, and policy documents
Track developments in biology, ML, and biosecurity for their potential to create new risks or enable new mitigations
Minimum qualifications
Strong proficiency in Python, and extensive background in scientific programming and data analysis skills
Excellent grasp of ML fundamentals and an ability to rapidly adopt ML development practices
Excellent knowledge of modern biology across both measurement and engineering: high-throughput assays and functional characterization, as well as gene synthesis, genome editing, strain construction, and protein engineering
Ability to build and maintain your own tooling rather than relying on others to implement your ideas
Experience designing quantitative experiments or evaluations and drawing defensible conclusions from noisy results
Strong analytical and writing skills, and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Familiarity with dual-use research concerns and biosecurity frameworks, such as select agent regulations, the Biological Weapons Convention, or Australia Group guidelines
Comfort with ambiguity and with shifting priorities as AI capabilities change
Can work independently while maintaining strong collaboration with cross-functional teams
Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Thrive in a fast-paced research environment where you balance rigorous scientific standards with rapid iteration
Preferred qualifications
Experience working with large language models, including prompting, fine-tuning, or evaluation
Experience training or deploying classifiers or other ML systems in production
Experience developing ML methods for biological systems or biological data
Familiarity with adversarial robustness, red-teaming, or safety evaluation of ML systems
Have at least 8 years of hands-on experience in life sciences, with deep expertise in areas such as molecular biology, drug discovery, or computational biology
Experience leading complex technical projects across multiple stakeholder groups

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

jobs.description: Are you ready to write code that operates real spacecraft in orbit? We're building the autonomous system that decides what every satellite in our constellation does, when it does it, and how it recovers when something goes wrong — all without a human in the loop for routine operations. This isn't about building another web service; it's about creating software that continuously manages an entire fleet of satellites at scale, making critical decisions under real physical constraints. This Senior role offers a rare combination: the depth of hard systems problems — planning and scheduling under physical constraints, coordinating across a large fleet, designing safeguards you have to trust with spacecraft — alongside the ownership that comes with a small team and an expanding charter. Because the constellation and its software are both still growing, the architecture decisions you make now will run for the life of the fleet, and your work connects directly to delivering reliable broadband to people who don't have it today. Export Control: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities - Work with our peer teams and customers to design suitable software systems to fulfill the mission needs. - Develop cloud native software systems in Java and Python. - Utilize AWS and other Amazon technologies to build highly-available software services. - Design and develop performant software systems that meet the mission criteria and requirements. - Help on-board and mentor new team members. - Lead technical roadmap definition efforts and decide which features and performance improvements to build. A day in the life You start the day with your team, aligning on what's shipping and where you can unblock each other. Most of your time goes to building: designing services, writing and reviewing code, and hardening systems that operate real spacecraft. You work closely with operators and mission teams, watching how they handle tricky situations, spotting patterns, and turning them into automation. Some weeks you go deep on a single system; others you're connecting several so they work as one. You'll also take turns supporting the systems you build, which keeps you close to how they behave in the real world. About the team Our mission is to operate a satellite constellation autonomously. We're building software that changes how satellites are managed: the ground sets the intent and guardrails, and the system schedules work, coordinates across the fleet, and recovers from faults on its own — with people supervising outcomes instead of issuing commands one at a time. We're a small team with a large and expanding charter, which means engineers here have real influence over architecture and direction. We care about operational excellence, clear thinking, and building systems we can trust with spacecraft. You'll collaborate closely with operations, mission planning, and hardware teams, and you'll see your work make a direct difference for customers who don't have reliable broadband today.

쿠팡은 고객 감동 실현을 위해 존재합니다. 고객들이 "쿠팡 없이 그동안 어떻게 살았을까?" 라고 말할 때, 비로소 우리의 미션을 실현하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 고객들의 쇼핑과 식사, 생활 전반을 편하게 만들겠다는 유일한 집념으로 쿠팡은 수억 달러 규모의 이커머스 산업 전반의 혁신을 이끌고 있습니다. 쿠팡은 가장 빠르게 성장하는 이커머스 기업 중 하나로, 국내 커머스 업계에서의 독보적인 입지와, 고객 신뢰를 구축했습니다.
쿠팡은 스타트업 문화를 기반으로 한 글로벌 대형 상장사라고 자부합니다. 이것이 창립 당시의 기민함을 유지하며, 신규 서비스를 끊임없이 출시하며 비즈니스를 확장해 나가는 우리의 성장 동력입니다. 쿠팡의 모든 임직원에게는 기업가 정신을 갖추고 새로운 혁신과 이니셔티브를 추진할 수 있는 기회가 주어집니다. 주저 없이 일에 뛰어들어 성과를 이루고자 하는 과감성이, 바로 쿠팡이 일하는 방식의 본질입니다. 쿠팡에서는 여러분 자신, 동료, 팀 그리고 회사 전체가 매일 성장하는 모습을 목격할 것입니다.

jobs.description: Come be a part of Amazon's dynamic Live Sports Production team. We are looking for an experienced Sr. Manager of Crewing to serve as the centralized crewing authority across all of our live sports properties. The Production Operations team is responsible for delivering high-quality event and studio productions on all global live sports properties to customers worldwide, across all Prime Video product lines and devices. We drive production excellence through streamlined processes and operational frameworks that empower the team to work more efficiently and grow with increasing demand. The growing volume and complexity across our properties demands a dedicated Sr. Manager of Crewing. This role provides the centralized coordination layer to ensure consistency, resolve conflicts, and maintain a unified view of crew availability across the entire Prime Video Live Sports portfolio and with third-party vendors. Our crewing operation is purpose-built around the needs of an expanding, multi-sport live portfolio rather than modeled after a traditional broadcast network structure. We are defining and building as we evolve, and this person must be excited to roll up their sleeves and help establish the systems, relationships, and workflows that will scale with us. This role requires deep knowledge of remote, event, and studio production crewing, including broadcast positions, industry standard rates, and an established network of relationships across production services. The Sr. Manager of Crewing will work in lockstep with property leads to ensure each event or studio show is properly staffed, communicating proactively with third-party partners to prevent gaps, resolve conflicts in real time, and keep productions on track. This role will also work closely with Amazon's internal legal and labor teams to ensure compliance with all applicable workforce regulations. The Sr. Manager of Crewing will be responsible for escalating issues that require senior leadership attention, keeping the Global Head of Production Operations informed on matters that carry risk or require resolution. Additionally, this person will partner directly with our Production Service Providers (PSP) to establish best practices, define operational standards for how PSPs engage with our productions, and ensure alignment on processes and expectations across the vendor landscape. The successful candidate is a self-starter who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment. You possess the ability to manage high volumes of tasks and projects quickly with autonomy, react with urgency to situations that demand immediate attention, and have a proven track record of end-to-end ownership in a fast-paced, dynamic business environment. Key job responsibilities • Cross-Property Crew Coordination & Visibility: Serve as the centralized coordination point across all live sports properties and studio productions, maintaining real-time visibility into crew availability, deployment, and engagement history to prevent scheduling conflicts. Work in lockstep with property leads to ensure every event and programming block is fully staffed with preferred, best-in-class personnel aligned to creative and editorial vision. • Real-Time Conflict Resolution: Identify and resolve crew conflicts in real time across overlapping productions, proactively scanning the production calendar to flag scheduling gaps and crewing risks well in advance of air. Coordinate with property leads to develop contingency plans and maintain a bench of qualified alternatives. • Rate Structure & Cost Consistency: Maintain organized, transparent rate structures across properties and personnel tiers, partnering with Production Ops and Production Managers leads to ensure alignment and consistency across comparable roles and production formats. Analyze crew spend patterns and maintain market-competitive positioning. Coordinate fee reconciliation and payment processing with third-party vendors across multiple properties to ensure accuracy and timeliness. Serve as a resource for property Production Operations and Production Management leads on market benchmarks and crew compensation norms to support informed planning decisions. • 3P Labor & Workforce Compliance: Serve as the primary point of contact for third-party labor questions. Navigate both union and non-union production environments, and ensure third-party PSPs adhere to all applicable labor regulations and collective bargaining agreements. Work closely with Amazon's internal legal and labor teams to stay current on regulatory requirements, labor guidelines, and workforce compliance standards across domestic and international markets. Advise property leads on compliance considerations as they arise, including crew classification, jurisdictional rules, and engagement terms. • Crew Scheduling & Resource Management: Ensure crew and resource scheduling across remote, studio, and third-party vendor operations stays aligned with property needs. Establish clear parameters and consistent frameworks for how personnel are deployed across productions. Recruit, negotiate, and onboard key Above-The-Line (ATL) and Below-The-Line (BTL) positions through PSPs as needed, establishing deal and rate frameworks, and engagement standards that apply uniformly across all properties. Maintain a centralized personnel repository, with the willingness to step in and coordinate travel and deployment logistics as production needs arise. • Systems, Tools & Reporting: Own and leverage internal production management tools to maintain full visibility into all productions and crew assignments, implementing and refining systems that map personnel to events, track availability, and surface conflicts. When needed, prepare and distribute crew communications (call sheets, playbooks, and pertinent production information) to stakeholders, and report on crewing metrics and workforce utilization to senior leadership.
